body.heading: Where in the world is Greece?
paragraphs: Greece is a country in Southern Europe, which is part of Europe.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of Greece is Athens.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: The language you will hear most in Greece is Greek.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of Greece is the euro. The euro is shared by many countries in Europe, so the same coins and notes work across borders.

body.heading: How big is Greece?
paragraphs: Greece covers about 132,000 square kilometres of land and inland water. That makes it about twice the size of Latvia.

body.heading: A fact to wow your friends
paragraphs: The Parthenon is an ancient temple on the Acropolis in Athens. The Parthenon was built for Athena, the goddess of wisdom, nearly 2,500 years ago — you can still see it glowing above Athens today.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: The Parthenon crowns the Acropolis, a marble temple built 2,500 years ago for the goddess Athena — the symbol of ancient Greece above a buzzing modern city.
Santorini's white villages cling to the rim of a drowned volcano, with blue domes, donkey paths and sunsets over the Aegean Sea.
